dose: 1 g combined EPA + DHA daily from fish oil or algal oil (check the label: a '1000 mg fish oil' capsule often has only 300 mg EPA+DHA). Taken with a meal containing fat.

summary.en: EPA and DHA are long-chain omega-3 fats that get built into cell membranes, especially in the heart, brain, retina and platelets, where they compete with omega-6 arachidonic acid and produce less inflammatory signalling molecules. At 1 g/day, blood triglycerides fall modestly (around 5–10%), platelets become slightly less sticky and the omega-3 index of red-cell membranes rises over 3–4 months. Big trials at this dose did not reduce heart attacks or strokes in the general population; the strong cardiovascular data are at 4 g/day of purified EPA in people with high triglycerides.
summary.hi: EPA और DHA लंबी चेन वाले ओमेगा-3 फ़ैट हैं जो कोशिकाओं की दीवार में जुड़ जाते हैं — ख़ासकर दिल, दिमाग़, आँख के रेटिना और प्लेटलेट्स में — और वहाँ ओमेगा-6 की जगह लेकर कम सूजन पैदा करने वाले सिग्नल बनाते हैं। रोज़ 1 ग्राम से ट्राइग्लिसराइड करीब 5–10% कम होते हैं, प्लेटलेट्स थोड़ी कम चिपचिपी होती हैं और 3–4 महीने में लाल कोशिकाओं का ओमेगा-3 लेवल बढ़ता है। इस डोज़ पर बड़ी स्टडीज़ में आम लोगों में हार्ट अटैक कम नहीं हुए; मज़बूत सबूत 4 ग्राम शुद्ध EPA पर, ज़्यादा ट्राइग्लिसराइड वालों में हैं।

indian_context: Most Indian diets, especially vegetarian ones, contain almost no EPA/DHA; the omega-3 that Indians do get is ALA from flaxseed (alsi), walnuts and mustard oil, of which the body converts only ~5–10% to EPA and under 1% to DHA. Indian omega-3 indices in studies are typically low (~3–4% vs an 8% target). High triglycerides with low HDL is the classic South Asian lipid pattern, which is exactly where omega-3 has its clearest effect. Fish oil capsules in India cost ₹5–15 per 1 g dose; algal DHA is the vegetarian option and is pricier.
sources: ASCEND Study Collaborative Group. Effects of n-3 fatty acid supplements in diabetes mellitus. N Engl J Med. 2018
Manson JE et al. Marine n-3 fatty acids and prevention of cardiovascular disease and cancer (VITAL). N Engl J Med. 2019
Bhatt DL et al. Cardiovascular risk reduction with icosapent ethyl for hypertriglyceridemia (REDUCE-IT). N Engl J Med. 2019
Skulas-Ray AC et al. Omega-3 fatty acids for the management of hypertriglyceridemia: a science advisory from the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2019
Gencer B et al. Effect of long-term marine omega-3 fatty acids supplementation on the risk of atrial fibrillation in randomized controlled trials. Circulation. 2021
caution: Safe for most adults at 1 g/day. Fishy burps and loose stools are the usual complaints. Tell your surgeon before an operation because clotting is slightly slowed. Anyone on warfarin or other blood thinners, or with a history of atrial fibrillation, should check with a doctor: higher doses (2–4 g) raise AF risk. Check for oxidation (rancid smell) and third-party purity testing for mercury and PCBs.

timeline.headline: Absorbed into blood lipids within hours; fishy aftertaste

effects.note: EPA/DHA are absorbed with fat via chylomicrons; plasma levels peak around 4–6 hours. Absorption roughly doubles when taken with a fatty meal versus empty stomach.
Fish oil floats on stomach contents, hence the fishy reflux. Enteric-coated capsules or taking it just before a meal reduces this.
Membrane composition of cells has not changed yet; the fat is circulating and being taken up into liver and tissues. No measurable effect today.

timeline.headline: Platelets slightly less sticky; triglycerides begin to dip

effects.note: EPA displaces arachidonic acid in platelet membranes, so less thromboxane A2 is made and platelets aggregate a little less readily. At 1 g the effect on bleeding time is small.
In the liver, omega-3s suppress SREBP-1c and reduce VLDL triglyceride secretion. Fasting triglycerides start falling within 1–2 weeks.
Loose stools in the first week are common as the gut adapts to the oil load; usually settles.

timeline.headline: Triglycerides down; membranes filling with omega-3

effects.note: One month in, the triglyceride reduction at 1 g/day is modest, roughly 5–10%, larger in people who started high. At 4 g/day the fall is 25–30%.
Omega-3 incorporates into heart-cell membranes, stabilising ion channels; resting heart rate typically drops a beat or two and heart-rate variability improves slightly.

Resolvins and protectins made from EPA/DHA quiet inflammatory signalling. Trials in rheumatoid arthritis show reduced morning stiffness and NSAID use, usually at doses above 2 g; at 1 g the effect is slight.

timeline.headline: Omega-3 index rising; joint and skin effects for some

effects.note: Red-cell membrane omega-3 index (EPA+DHA as % of fatty acids) has climbed from a typical Indian ~3–4% toward 5–6%. A small drop in blood pressure (~1–2 mmHg) appears in meta-analyses at this stage.
Skin barrier lipids shift toward omega-3; some people with dry skin or mild eczema notice less itch. Evidence is limited and inconsistent.
DHA is the dominant fat in the retina and in meibomian gland secretions. Dry-eye trials are mixed; the large DREAM trial found no benefit over olive oil placebo.

timeline.headline: Steady state; brain, retina and sperm membranes enriched

effects.note: After ~4 months (a red-cell lifetime), the omega-3 index has reached its new plateau. An index above 8% is associated with lower cardiac death in cohorts; 1 g/day gets most Indians to about 6–7%, not 8%.

DHA is 10–15% of brain fatty acids and turns over slowly; six months enriches it. Effects on mood are real but small, mostly in clinical depression with EPA-rich formulas; no measurable gain in memory in healthy adults.
Sperm membranes are DHA-rich. Meta-analyses show modest improvement in sperm motility and count with omega-3 supplementation in subfertile men over 3–6 months.

timeline.headline: One year: the honest outcome data at this dose

effects.note: In ASCEND (15,000 diabetics) and VITAL (25,000 adults), 1 g/day for 5–7 years did not reduce major cardiovascular events overall. VITAL did see fewer heart attacks in people who ate little fish, which describes many Indians, but this was a secondary finding.
Triglyceride lowering holds as long as you keep taking it. In fatty liver disease, omega-3 modestly reduces liver fat in meta-analyses, but far less than losing 5–7% body weight does.
The AF signal in trials is dose-dependent: clear at 4 g/day, not significant at 1 g, but not zero. A person with prior atrial fibrillation should know this.

timeline.headline: Five years: safe, modest metabolic benefit, no proven life extension

effects.note: Long-term omega-3 keeps triglycerides and platelet reactivity slightly better than they would be; population cohorts with higher omega-3 index have lower cardiac mortality, but supplement trials at 1 g have not proven that the pill delivers it.

Long-term trials (VITAL-Cog, AREDS2) show no cognitive protection from omega-3 in older adults. Eating fish twice a week tracks better with brain outcomes than capsules, likely because of what fish replaces.
Five years of daily EPA/DHA modestly lowers inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6). No harm to immune function has been shown at this dose.
